page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is a KVM-hypervised virtual server configured with 4 shared vCPUs and 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.0 GB of RAM per core. The underlying processor is an AMD EPYC 7542 x86_64 architecture CPU operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor features 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1d cache. It supports hardware-level instructions such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2. No local storage or dedicated GPU resources are bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates that the shared CPU allocation impacts raw compute performance. The instance registers a stress-ng single-core score of 780.79 and a multi-core score of 3123.05. Geekbench testing aligns with this, showing an average single-core score of 1200.0 but a weak multi-core score of 3876.0. Memory bandwidth is mixed; cached small-block reads reach an average of 411.67 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block reads drop to a weak 36.0 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput are also positioned in the bottom 25 percent. However, the server maintains average performance in Redis SET operations at 5.87 million operations per second and single-threaded compression tasks.

Given its shared CPU architecture and moderate compute benchmarks, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require a larger memory footprint relative to CPU power but do not demand sustained, high-performance compute. It is well-suited for lightweight web serving, background task processing, Redis caching, and small-scale development environments. It is less suitable for CPU-intensive tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, or medium-to-large language model inference, where benchmarks show poor to weak execution speeds.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is an x86_64 virtual server featuring 4 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs and 24.0 GB of RAM, running on the KVM hypervisor. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks reflect its shared CPU allocation, with stress-ng single-core compute scoring in the bottom 10% and multi-core in the bottom 25%. However, it maintains average performance in cached memory reads at 411.67 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 5.87 million operations per second. This resource profile provides a cost-effective option for memory-leaning workloads that do not require continuous, high-intensity CPU utilization. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, caching layers, and lightweight web serving, while intensive tasks like software compilation or large-scale database operations may experience performance bottlenecks due to shared compute constraints.
